per-chileus: A man of Tegea who held great influence with the Lacedaemonians and persuaded the ephors to heed the Athenian delegation's warnings against the Persian invasion.
per-pleistarchus: King of Sparta, son of Leonidas, too young to command the army at Plataea and thus represented by his guardian Pausanias.
per-olympiodorus: Athenian commander of three hundred picked men sent to relieve the Megarians at Plataea during the final battle against the Persians.
per-androcrates: A Plataean hero with a precinct near the Gargaphian spring, where the Greek forces encamped before the Battle of Plataea.
per-macistius: Persian cavalry commander under Mardonius, known for his prowess and mounted on an ornate Nesaean horse, killed while leading charges against the Greeks at Plataea.
per-argaeus: Macedonian king, ancestor of Perdiccas and progenitor of the royal line that produced Alexander and Amyntas.
per-hieronymus: An athlete of Andros who nearly defeated Tisamenus in a wrestling match at Olympia.
per-clytiadae: A clan (genos) within the Iamid line, to which the Elean diviner Tisamenus belonged.
per-clytiad: A clan within the Iamid family of diviners, to which the Elean soothsayer Tisamenus belonged.
per-hegias: Brother of Tisamenus the Elean diviner, granted Spartan citizenship on the same terms as his brother in exchange for their family's services to Lacedaemon during the Persian Wars.
per-hippomachus: A diviner from Leucas who worked for the Greeks with Mardonius' army and attempted to obtain favorable omens before the battle at Plataea.
per-phegeus: Grandfather of Echemus, king of Tegea, in the legendary conflict against Hyllus and the Heraclidae.
per-echemus: Tegean general and king, son of Eeropus, who in antiquity fought and defeated Hyllus in single combat to prevent the Heraclidae's return to the Peloponnese, thereby earning the Tegeans the right to hold the second wing in all united Peloponnesian campaigns.
per-eeropus: A king of Tegea and father of Echemus, who won the right to the second position in Peloponnesian armies by his son's victory in single combat against Hyllus the Heraclid.
per-timagenides: Timagenides, son of Herpys, was a Theban who advised Mardonius to guard the Cithaeron pass to intercept incoming Greek reinforcements during the Plataean campaign.
per-herpys: Father of Timagenides, a Theban who advised Mardonius during the Persian campaign.
per-poliades: Father of Amompharetus, a Spartan officer who led the Pitanate battalion at Plataea.
per-aeimnestus: A Spartan of note who killed the Persian general Mardonius at Plataea and later died leading three hundred men against Messenia at Stenyclerus.
per-thrasydeius: Brother of Thorax of Larissa and Eurypylus, a Thessalian of the house of Aleuas whom Mardonius rebukes for praising Lacedaemonian warriors at Plataea.
per-aleuas: Father of Thorax of Larissa and his brothers Eurypylus and Thrasydeius, Thessalian allies of Mardonius whom the Persian general reproaches for their earlier assurances about Spartan martial prowess.
per-asopodorus: Theban cavalry commander, son of Timander, who charged the Megarians and Philasians as they approached in disorder during the rout at Plataea.
per-timander: A Theban, father of Asopodorus who led Theban horsemen at Plataea.
per-eurypylus: Brother of Thorax of Larissa and Thrasydeus, and son of Aleuas; a Thessalian whom Mardonius rebukes for having praised Lacedaemonian military prowess before the Battle of Plataea.
per-eutychides: Father of Sophanes of Decelea, an Athenian who gained renown at the battle of Plataea.
per-arimnestus: A Plataean to whom the dying Spartan Callicrates expressed his regret at not having struck a blow in the battle of Plataea.
per-decelus: A man of Decelea who, according to some accounts, revealed Helen's location to the Tyndaridae because he resented Theseus's pride, earning the Deceleans perpetual privileges at Sparta.
per-titacus: One of the autochthonoi who handed over the town of Aphidnae to the Tyndaridae in the mythical past.
per-dionysophanes: An Ephesian said by some to have removed and buried the body of Mardonius after the Battle of Plataea.
per-autodicus: A Plataean, father of Cleades, who served as patron and protector to the Aeginetans.
per-antagoras: A Coan, father of Hegetorides and grandfather of the concubine of the Persian Pharandates who supplicated Pausanias after Plataea.
per-cleades: A Plataean, son of Autodicus, who built a cenotaph for the Aeginetans at Plataea ten years after the battle.
per-leagrus: An Athenian general who served alongside Sophanes in a campaign at Datus against the Edonians over gold-mines.
per-glaucon: Son of Glaucon and colleague of the Athenian general Sophanes.
per-athenagoras: A Samian envoy, son of Archestratides, sent with Lampon and Hegesistratus to urge the Greek fleet under Leutychides to attack the Persians at Mykale.
per-archestratides: The father of Athenagoras, a Samian envoy sent to the Greek fleet under Leutychides at Delos to encourage action against the Persians at Mykale.
per-philistus: Founder of a temple of Eleusinian Demeter at Mykale, who accompanied Nileus son of Codrus in the colonization of Miletus.
per-pasicles: Father of Philistus, who founded a temple of Eleusinian Demeter at Mykale when accompanying Nileus son of Codrus to the founding of Miletus.
per-nileus: Son of Codrus; founder of Miletus according to Herodotus' account of its colonial settlement.
per-themsitocles: An Athenian strategos who devised a similar psychological stratagem at Artemisium of addressing enemy Greeks to undermine Persian confidence.
per-ithanitres: A Persian admiral of the fleet who escaped during the final Greek assault on the Persian defensive wall at Plataea.
per-perilaus: A general of Sicyon killed in the Battle of Mycale while fighting against the Persians.
per-euthoenus: Father of Hermolycus, an Athenian pancratium wrestler who distinguished himself in the battle at Plataea.
per-praxilaus: Father of Xenagoras of Halicarnassus, who saved Masistes from Artayntes' sword at Mykale.
per-thrasycles: Lampon of Thrasycles was a Samian messenger sent secretly by Samos to the Greek fleet at Delos to encourage them to attack the Persian forces at Mykale.
per-hebe: A battle-cry meaning "youth" or "vigor," proclaimed by the Greek commander Leutychides to rally the Ionians at Mykale against Persian forces.
per-iphiclus: Father of Protesilaus, a Greek hero who was the first to fall in the Trojan War and whose shrine in the Chersonesus was plundered by Artayctes.
per-plistorus: A god worshipped by the Apsinthians of Thrace, to whom they sacrificed the Persian Oeobazus in their customary manner.
